key_insight: Task-defined spectral queries steer how parameterized quantum circuits combine existing signal frequencies, creating task-aligned inductive biases without adding sample-dependent information.
engineering_relevance: Known spectral structure can guide quantum circuit design for data-limited classification, including radar-like tasks performed before image formation.
method: Use data-reuploading circuits with a sample-varying signal and a fixed, task-defined spectral query.
Align query encoding with nonuniform Fourier evaluation frequencies and sampling positions.
Compare aligned queries against parameter-matched circuits with mismatched or absent queries.
evidence_signal: Across small-scale spectral and synthetic-aperture-radar-inspired classification tasks, aligned queries improved learning from limited data over parameter-matched baselines.
watch_item: Small-scale results do not establish scalability, robustness on noisy quantum hardware, or advantage over classical methods.
paper_title: Task-aligned spectral inductive biases in parameterized quantum circuits
